305128: The report identified several Yelp functions that were vulnerable to clickjacking attacks, including reporting a user profile, following a user, and sending a compliment. The impact of these vulnerabilities was that they could have affected user interactions on the Yelp platform. To mitigate these attacks, Yelp deployed a site-wide CSP policy.
355859: The Yelp Reservations page was vulnerable to clickjacking attacks. The lack of the X-Frame-Options header in the response headers allowed malicious actors to embed the reservation page as a hidden iframe on their own website. When a victim visited the attacker's website and interacted with the embedded iframe, their email address and other private information was disclosed to the attacker without their knowledge or consent.
358143: The Insecure Direct Object Reference vulnerability allowed an attacker to associate a randomly added but deregistered credit card with their own account via the /rewards/signup endpoint. The vulnerability was quickly validated and fixed by Yelp.
361984:
The summary is as follows:

A vulnerability was discovered that allowed an attacker to obtain the last four digits of a credit card registered with the Yelp platform. This was achieved through the error messages returned by the `/profile_payment/save` endpoint.
391092: The researcher discovered an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability that allowed an attacker to use someone else's registered credit card to order food through the Grubhub platform on Yelp. No credit card information was disclosed as a result of this vulnerability. The vulnerability was reported to and addressed by the Yelp security team.
391385: The reported vulnerability allowed an attacker to overlay the Yelp checkout page, potentially resulting in unauthorized credit card charges for the victim. Yelp deployed mitigations to prevent such clickjacking attacks.
664038: The protected tweet settings were overwritten by other settings without the account owner's knowledge. The vulnerability allowed the account's tweets to become unprotected, despite the owner having enabled the protected tweets setting on the mobile.twitter.com website.
727870: The WordPress installation at the marketing site www.yoti.com was found to have an issue where user information of administrative accounts was publicly accessible through an accessible WordPress REST API endpoint. Sensitive information about administrator accounts, including usernames, was exposed without any authentication or special permissions required.
738615: A vulnerability was discovered in Yoti's marketing website (www.yoti.com) WordPress implementation. The vulnerability exposed admin usernames through WordPress API endpoints.
761000: A vulnerability was discovered that enabled account takeover of millions of MTN user accounts due to a lack of rate limiting when sending OTP codes, allowing attackers to brute force the codes.
774050: The vulnerability allowed an attacker to flood the victim's email inbox with Yelp confirmation emails due to the absence of rate limiting in the email resend functionality. The vulnerability was present in the URL https://biz.yelp.com/welcome/resend_confirmation.
777957:
The summary is as follows:

A vulnerability was discovered where the request that sends the one-time password (OTP) to authenticate subscribers also returns the OTP in the network response, allowing an attacker to bypass the OTP prompt and manage users' subscriptions.
868146: An account modification vulnerability was found that allowed unauthorized changes to user details. The issue was demonstrated by intercepting and modifying requests to change account information like nickname and date of birth. This could lead to sensitive data exposure and identity theft. Fixing this vulnerability is strongly recommended.
906907: The vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to other users' profile pictures and associated geolocation data, which was not properly stripped from the uploaded images. An attacker could exploit this issue to retrieve sensitive information about other users.
932557: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was found in the LinkedIn URL field within the 'Buddies-to-Be' section of a campaign. User input was not properly sanitized, allowing malicious scripts to be executed when the LinkedIn icon was clicked. This could lead to unauthorized actions or access to sensitive user data.
946053: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered after a payload placed years ago in a test site triggered in an internal administration panel, alerting the company to the issue. Upon review, a maximum bounty was awarded under the cross-site scripting category due to the security impact of the payload executing internally.
965141: The vulnerability allowed the removal of reviews through clickjacking. The review removal functionality was accessible within an iframe.
985367: A weak password policy in the signup process led to password leakage and account takeovers. The vulnerability was fixed.
996371: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was reported in the "My Custom Rule" field at a template editor, which could allow malicious scripts to be embedded. The issue was addressed.
1010466: The vulnerability allowed for a blind cross-site scripting (XSS) attack on the image upload functionality. The filename parameter was not properly sanitized, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code that would execute when the image was displayed. This vulnerability could be exploited via a CSRF attack to send a malicious image to the support chat, potentially affecting multiple users.
1011767: The X-Forwarded-For header was found to allow bypassing access restrictions on the Business Owner App backend API. By setting this header to 127.0.0.1, the responding server was tricked into believing the request came from an internal IP address, granting access to restricted endpoints that would otherwise be inaccessible.
1025365: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was reported in the "Section Name" field of the "Accordion" block element. Malicious scripts could potentially be injected and executed in the context of users' browsers through this field. The issue has since been resolved.
1029723: A vulnerability was found where there was no rate limiting for subscribing emails, which could lead to cross origin misconfiguration. The issue was resolved.
1037714: A cross-site scripting vulnerability was found in the email input on the intensedebate.com user account edit page. The email input failed to sanitize user-supplied data, allowing JavaScript code to be injected. This could enable an attacker to execute malicious scripts in a victim's browser within the security context of the intensedebate.com domain.
